name: US Visa Appointment Watcher
description: Slot availability, target windows and watcher health. Metrics are pushed by app/newrelic.py after every sweep. IMPORTANT: replace every accountIds value 8461506 with your own New Relic account ID before importing -- the import dialog does not do it for you. Run: python monitoring/render-dashboard.py <your-account-id>

pages.name: Overview
pages.description: Where the earliest slot sits, per application and consulate. All charts follow the time picker; set it to 7 days for the trends to mean anything.

nrqlQueries.query: FROM Metric SELECT latest(usvisa.earliest_slot_days) AS 'Now' FACET application, consulate LIMIT 20

widgets.title: Best ever offered in this window
widgets.description: min() across the whole picker range. If this is far below the value on the left, an earlier slot appeared and was taken before the next sweep.

nrqlQueries.query: FROM Metric SELECT min(usvisa.earliest_slot_days) AS 'Best seen' FACET application, consulate LIMIT 20
FROM Metric SELECT latest(usvisa.applications_count) AS 'Watched', max(usvisa.matches_count) AS 'Matched', latest(usvisa.booked_count) AS 'Booked'
FROM Metric SELECT latest(usvisa.worker_running) AS 'Worker', min(usvisa.account_login_ok) AS 'Login', latest(usvisa.sweeps_total) AS 'Sweeps'
FROM Metric SELECT max(usvisa.seconds_since_check) AS 'Since last poll'

widgets.title: Earliest slot offered — min per bucket, so brief dips survive
widgets.description: min() rather than latest(): a slot that appears for one sweep and is taken before the next would be invisible with latest().

nrqlQueries.query: FROM Metric SELECT min(usvisa.earliest_slot_days) FACET application, consulate TIMESERIES AUTO

FROM Metric SELECT latest(usvisa.earliest_slot_days) AS 'Now (d)', min(usvisa.earliest_slot_days) AS 'Best (d)', min(usvisa.earliest_acceptable_slot_days) AS 'In window (d)', latest(usvisa.available_days) AS 'Offered' FACET application, consulate LIMIT 50

widgets.title: Movement — days gained per day (negative = slots moving earlier)

nrqlQueries.query: FROM Metric SELECT derivative(usvisa.earliest_slot_days, 1 day) FACET consulate TIMESERIES AUTO
FROM Metric SELECT max(usvisa.available_days) FACET consulate TIMESERIES AUTO
FROM Metric SELECT min(usvisa.target_deadline_days) FACET application TIMESERIES AUTO

rawConfiguration.text:
### How to read it

**Set the time picker (top right) to `Last 7 days`.** Every chart here follows it — New Relic's picker supersedes any `SINCE` in a query, so none of these queries pin their own window. The trend and Movement charts need more than a day of history to say anything.

**`min()`, not `latest()`.** `earliest_slot_days` is sampled every `poll_interval`. A chart bucket holds several samples, and `latest()` would keep only the last one — so a slot that appeared for a single sweep and was taken before the next would vanish from the graph. `min()` keeps the dip, which is the whole event worth seeing. The one place `latest()` is used is the *right now* tile, where the current state is the question.

**"Now" far above "Best seen"** means an earlier slot did appear during the window and is already gone. If that keeps happening well inside your target window, the bot is losing races and `poll_interval` is too slow.

**Day counts are computed when each point is pushed.** A point from a month ago means "this many days out *as of then*", which is what makes the trend meaningful — but only the newest point literally means "from today".

**A blank `In window (d)`** means nothing has ever fallen inside your `earliest/latest_acceptable_date` — normal, not missing data. **A consulate absent entirely** returned zero availability: metrics are omitted rather than sent as `0`, because `0` would read as "a slot is free today". Use `usvisa.consulate_status` (`status` = `none` / `out-of-window` / `match` / `error`) and `usvisa.consulate_poll_ok` to tell "nothing free" from "request failed".

nrqlQueries.query: FROM Metric SELECT max(usvisa.sweeps_total) TIMESERIES AUTO

widgets.title: Login and worker status — min(), so any blip shows

nrqlQueries.query: FROM Metric SELECT min(usvisa.account_login_ok) AS 'Login OK', min(usvisa.worker_running) AS 'Worker running', min(usvisa.up) AS 'Reporting' TIMESERIES AUTO
FROM Metric SELECT max(usvisa.seconds_since_check) FACET application TIMESERIES AUTO
FROM Metric SELECT count(usvisa.consulate_status) AS 'Samples' FACET application, consulate, status LIMIT 100
FROM Metric SELECT count(usvisa.application_state) AS 'Samples' FACET account, application, schedule_id, state LIMIT 100
FROM NrIntegrationError SELECT timestamp, category, message, name LIMIT 50
FROM Metric SELECT count(*) AS 'Data points' WHERE metricName LIKE 'usvisa.%' FACET metricName LIMIT 50
